newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK sites seen drawing keen interest in auction.
newsitem.headline: HK sites seen drawing keen interest in auction.

text.p: Two major Hong Kong residential sites are expected to draw keen interest at a government land auction next Tuesday, the last to be held before the territory's handover to China, property analysts said.

The auction, a key confidence indicator in the local property market and economy before Britain returns Hong Kong to China on July 1, is expected to draw the participation of big guns in the property sector and fetch up to HK$12.3 billion.

A 571,848 square-foot site in beachside Stanley on southern Hong Kong island is expected to sell for between HK$6.4 billion and HK$7.3 billion in the auction, the first in the 1997-98 financial year (April-March), analysts said on Thursday.
Serena Lau, managing director at Francis Lau & Co (Surveyors), said the site is likely to be used to build villas.

"This kind of property is currently in great demand. Their prices have been rising to ever new heights. Therefore the site will attract the bidding of big developers," said Lau, who expected a selling price of HK$6.43 billion for the site.
Another 79,675 sq ft waterfront site in Kowloon's Hunghom is tipped to fetch HK$4 billion to HK$5 billion, analysts said.
William Wong, director in valuation and consultancy at First Pacific Davies, said he expected the selling price to be HK$4.2 billion, judging from the current prices in the district.
The site is next to Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd's Laguna Verde residential development, whose offer of flats have recently attracted an enthusiastic response.
Sentiment has been bullish in the property market. Prices have rebounded more than 10 percent since the government announced measures in March to curb property prices, analysts said.
The announcement had brought about a fall of about 10-12 percent in the luxury residential sector, and five to seven percent in the mass residential market, analysts said.
"Sentiment is quite good," Lau said. She attributed the latest price bounce to fundamental demand in the market from both end-users and investors.
She said the buoyant sentiment could help the sites fetch higher prices.
Major developers including Cheung Kong, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, CITIC Pacific Ltd and Hang Lung Development Co Ltd have reportedly declared interest in bidding for the sites.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd, and Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd are also expected to take part, analysts said.
"The auction will draw interest from big players because the sites are big," Lau said. "There isn't enough supply of residential land. So the interest is there."

Also on sale at Tuesday's auction will be a small 24,111-sq-ft residential site on Lantau Island, where the territory's new airport is being built. A selling price between HK$11 million and HK$30 million is expected.
"As it involves a relatively low price, quite a number of small developers are also expected to bid," said Lau, who estimated a selling price of HK$21.50 million for the site.
